title: Show hidden connections: how two pieces of a scan are joined, and the ring that would separate them
description:
User report 2026-10-04: on the repaired crawfish it is often impossible to see that two parts are connected at all (e.g. through bridges that repair_mesh or the scan created), so rings and regions behave unexpectedly. Wanted: a tool where the user clicks two places (or two regions) and is shown the shortest surface path between them, highlighting thin bridges, and optionally the smallest ring that would disconnect them. Also consider a mode that highlights every thin neck/bridge below a size relative to its surroundings, and which connections repair_mesh introduced (its filled holes are already reported by mesh-holes).

Raised to priority 1 after the crawfish segmentation review (2026-10-04): the main shell has genus 17 because the scan fused limbs to the body, and 43 of the user's 82 rings separate nothing for that reason. A fused bridge (a handle) needs a second cut across it; the user tried tiny rings at contact points (ring_16, ring_22, ring_58, ring_59). The separating-ring suggestion here should handle handles: find the bridge and offer the cut that actually disconnects.

Correction 2026-10-04 to the note above: '43 rings separate nothing' overstated it. RingRegions tests each ring alone (it floods the surface with only that ring's edges as walls, RingRegions.java ~255-318): 43 of the 82 rings do not cut the surface in two on their own because the loop goes around a handle (the main shell has genus 17 from scan fusion), so they get no distal/proximal side. In the real split, with all rings as walls, they still act as walls and bound regions; whether each one ends up with different regions on its two sides was not measured. The consequence is narrower: a handle ring has no distal side of its own (which matters to anything that picks 'the distal side' of a ring), and a limb fused elsewhere needs a second cut before the limb comes free.

Rework 2026-10-06 (user review): the minimum-cut (magenta) loop usually just circles one of the picks, so it is not useful; the narrowest cross-section (green) is the one the user wants, because it sits at the actual neck. Keep the green one as the only suggestion shown, snapped to mesh edges so it can be confirmed as a ring; drop the minimum cut from the tool. The picks are surface anchors like the ring tool's (hover highlight, grab near one to drag it, the connection re-runs on release), reusing the ring tool's anchor code rather than a copy. After Enter, the confirmed ring opens in the ring tool for editing (reopenRing, CRAW-47).
definition-of-done:
1. Click two points: the connecting surface path is drawn and its narrowest point marked. 2. The minimal separating ring is offered as a draft the user can confirm. 3. repair_mesh-created connections can be shown. 4. Works on the full crawfish scan interactively.

SurfaceConnection.pathFilledFaceCount (repair_mesh fill faces the connecting path crosses) stays: it is the item-3 answer the connection tool and route report.

Rework: 5. Only the narrowest cross-section is shown as the suggestion (plus the path), snapped to mesh edges; the minimum-cut loops are gone from the tool, and MinimumCut is deleted if nothing else uses it. 6. Enter confirms that loop as a ring and switches to the ring tool with it open for editing. 7. The two picks are anchors: hover highlight, press near one and drag to move it, re-run on release; the anchor picking and drag code is shared with RingTool, not duplicated. 8. Overlay colours are named Color constants and the status line names what each colour is. 9. On the crawfish, picking either side of a limb joint confirms a ring at the joint, not around a pick.

10. Enter confirms the green cross-section and switches straight to the ring edit tool with that ring already selected as the draft, its anchors ready to move, with no extra click.

Clarified 2026-10-06 (user), item 6: Enter confirms the green edge-snapped neck and goes straight to the ring tool with the new ring already open as the draft, its anchors ready to drag, add and delete; no extra click.
testing-plan: 1. Unit test on two spheres joined by a thin tube: path goes through the tube, separating ring sits on it. 2. Live on the crawfish where the user found a hidden join.
changes-made: New Connection tool (Ctrl+J) in the ring-tool scene: click two places to see the shortest surface path between them, the narrowest cross-section on it, and the minimum set of loops that separates them (minimum cut on the face graph, priced by edge length). A handle gets two loops. Enter confirms the loops as unsaved rings in the ring tool. By default the existing rings act as walls (W toggles this). repair_mesh now records which faces its hole filling added (MeshRepairReport.fillFaceIndices); F colours them, and the path and loops report how many they touch. New automation route: connection. Crawfish (938k faces): face graph 135 ms, path 0.2-0.3 s, cut 0.5-0.7 s. Tests: SurfaceConnectionTest (dumbbell tube, pinched-torus handle) and a MeshRepairTest fill-face check.

Rework 2026-10-06: the connection tool (Ctrl+J) now shows only the shortest path (yellow) and the narrowest cross-section on it (green), snapped to mesh edges as a closed vertex loop; the minimum cut and its magenta loops are gone and MinimumCut is deleted. Enter confirms the green loop through the new RingTool.confirmLoop (anchors fitted to the loop, one undoable edit, unsaved ring), switches to the ring tool and reopens it as the draft (reopenRing), anchors ready to drag, add and delete. The two picks are anchors: cyan, white under the cursor, press near one and drag, the connection re-runs on release. Cursor picking (pickCursor), anchor hit-testing (anchorUnderCursor) and worldPerPixel moved from RingTool into RingScene and both tools use them; RingTool's graph-ring fit became fitLoop, shared by graph-ring conversion and confirmLoop. Overlay colours are Color.CONNECTION_PATH/NECK/PICK/PICK_HOVERED/REPAIR_FILL and the status line names each. Rings as walls (W) and repair_mesh fills (F) stay. Crawfish (938k faces): face graph 127 ms, path 0.1-0.2 s, cross-sections 10-180 ms; a sweep picking either side of each of the user's rings put the neck at the joint for 18 of 25 rings with distinct sides (ring_05/06/11/13/14/18/30/33/34/36-38/40-42/44-46), off for 7 (ring_00/03/04/07/23/31/32, the neck drifting toward a pick). Live Enter: ring 82 from neck, 9 authored anchors, 248 edges, open as the draft. Tests: SurfaceConnectionTest (dumbbell: neck is an edge loop on the tube that separates the spheres), Ring*Test, MeshRepairTest; full suite 440 green.
